label: October 2026
desc: Starter: polite phrases and friendly everyday words.
Everyday formal verbs and casual chat.
Formal email language and relaxed British English.
Academic adjectives and common informal expressions.
Advanced formal words and business idioms.
Rare formal vocabulary and expressive idioms.

words.def: A polite greeting you use between about 12 o'clock and 6 o'clock.
words.ex: Good afternoon, can I help you?
words.ex2: The teacher said good afternoon to the class.
words.watch: Use good afternoon to say hello, not goodbye. To say goodbye, say Have a nice afternoon.
words.prompt: Greet a receptionist at 2 pm and say why you are there.
words.model: Good afternoon. I have a meeting with Ms Nowak at half past two.
qs: Who do you say good afternoon to at work or school?
What do you usually do in the afternoon?

up.model: Good afternoon. How can I help you?

pl: Grzeczne powitanie używane mniej więcej od 12 do 18.
ro: bună ziua
Salut politicos folosit cam de la ora 12 până la ora 18.

words.def: A polite greeting you use after about 6 o'clock in the evening.
words.ex: Good evening and welcome to the show.
words.ex2: The waiter said good evening and gave us the menu.
words.watch: Good evening is a greeting. Good night is what you say when you leave or go to bed.
words.prompt: Greet guests at a dinner party in a polite way.
words.model: Good evening, everyone. Thank you for coming tonight.
qs: Where do people say good evening to you?
What time does the evening start for you?

pl: Grzeczne powitanie używane mniej więcej po 18.
ro: bună seara
Salut politicos folosit cam după ora 18.

words.def: A polite question you ask when you meet someone, to show interest in them.
words.ex: Hello, Mr Smith. How are you today?
words.ex2: She always asks how are you before the lesson starts.
words.watch: The usual answer is short: Fine, thanks. And you? Don't give a long story to a stranger.
words.prompt: Start a phone call with a colleague politely.
words.model: Hello, Anna, it's Tomasz. How are you?
qs: How do you usually answer how are you?
Is how are you a real question in your language?

pl: jak się masz? / jak się Pan/Pani miewa?
Grzeczne pytanie przy spotkaniu, by okazać zainteresowanie.
ro: ce mai faceți? / ce mai faci?
Întrebare politicoasă când întâlnești pe cineva, ca să arăți interes.

words.def: Something you say to greet a person who has just arrived.
words.ex: Welcome to our school!
words.ex2: The hotel staff welcomed us with a smile.
words.watch: Say welcome to + a place: Welcome to Poland. Thank you is answered with you're welcome, not with welcome.
words.prompt: Say hello to a new student in your class.
words.model: Hi, welcome to our class! My name is Ola.
qs: How do people welcome guests in your home?
Which country gave you the warmest welcome?

pl: Słowo, którym witasz kogoś, kto właśnie przyszedł.
ro: bine ai venit / bine ați venit
Ce spui ca să saluți pe cineva care tocmai a sosit.

words.def: A polite way to say yes when someone asks for something.
words.ex: Can I sit here? Of course.
words.ex2: Of course you can use my pen.
words.watch: Be careful: of course can sound rude after a question with an obvious answer. Use it for requests.
words.prompt: Someone asks to borrow your book. Answer politely.
words.model: Of course, here you are.
qs: What do you always say yes to?
What would you never say of course to?

pl: Grzeczny sposób, by powiedzieć tak na czyjąś prośbę.
ro: desigur
Un mod politicos de a spune da când cineva îți cere ceva.

words.def: A very polite way to say yes, often used by people who serve customers.
words.ex: Could I have the bill, please? Certainly.
words.ex2: I will certainly call you tomorrow.
words.watch: Certainly sounds more formal than sure. Shop assistants and waiters use it a lot.
words.prompt: You work in a café. A customer asks for water. Answer.
words.model: Certainly. Still or sparkling?
qs: Who says certainly to you most often?
What will you certainly do this weekend?

pl: Bardzo grzeczny sposób, by powiedzieć tak, często używany przez obsługę.
ro: desigur, cu siguranță
Un mod foarte politicos de a spune da, folosit des de cei care servesc clienții.

words.def: A very polite way to ask if you are allowed to do something.
words.ex: May I open the window?
words.ex2: Excuse me, may I ask you a question?
words.watch: After may I, use the base verb: May I sit here? Not: May I to sit here?
words.prompt: Ask your teacher politely if you can leave the room.
words.model: Excuse me, may I go to the toilet, please?
qs: When do you use may I instead of can I?
What did you ask permission for as a child?

pl: Bardzo grzeczny sposób, by zapytać o pozwolenie.
ro: pot să…? / îmi permiteți să…?
Un mod foarte politicos de a cere voie.

words.def: A polite way to start a request when you ask someone to do something.
words.ex: Could you close the door, please?
words.ex2: Could you tell me the way to the station?
words.watch: Could you is more polite than can you. Add please at the end for extra politeness.
words.prompt: Ask a stranger to take a photo of you.
words.model: Excuse me, could you take a photo of us, please?
qs: What do you often ask other people to do for you?
Who do you find it hard to ask for help?

up.model: Could you help me with this, please?

pl: Grzeczny początek prośby, gdy prosisz kogoś o zrobienie czegoś.
ro: ați putea…? / ai putea…?
Un început politicos de cerere, când rogi pe cineva să facă ceva.

words.def: What you say to tell someone who you are.
coll: my name is … and I'm from …
words.ex: Good morning, my name is Anna Kowalska.
words.ex2: My name is Radu and I'm from Cluj.
words.watch: In English we say my name is Anna, not I am called Anna in most situations. With friends, just say I'm Anna.
words.prompt: Introduce yourself at a job interview.
words.model: Good morning. My name is Piotr Zając and I'm here for the interview.
qs: What does your name mean?
Do you like your name? Why?

pl: To, co mówisz, by przedstawić się innej osobie.
ro: mă numesc
Ce spui ca să-i spui cuiva cine ești.

words.def: A question you use to ask about a price or an amount.
words.ex: How much is this jacket?
words.ex2: How much does a ticket to London cost?
words.watch: Use how much with prices and with things you can't count (how much water). Use how many with things you can count (how many apples).
words.prompt: Ask a shop assistant about the price of two things.
words.model: Excuse me, how much are these shoes and how much is the bag?
qs: How much does a coffee cost where you live?
How much time do you spend on your phone?

pl: Pytanie o cenę albo o ilość.
ro: cât (costă)?
Întrebare despre preț sau despre o cantitate.

words.def: What you say when you cannot follow what someone has said.
words.ex: Sorry, I don't understand. Could you say it again?
words.ex2: I don't understand this word.
words.watch: Say I don't understand, not I'm not understanding, in most situations.
words.prompt: Someone speaks to you too fast. Tell them politely.
words.model: Sorry, I don't understand. Could you speak more slowly, please?
qs: What is difficult to understand in English for you?
What do you do when you don't understand a word?

pl: To, co mówisz, gdy nie wiesz, co ktoś powiedział.
ro: nu înțeleg
Ce spui când nu poți urmări ce a spus cineva.

words.def: To say or do something again.
words.ex: Could you repeat that, please?
words.ex2: The teacher repeated the new word three times.
words.watch: Say repeat, not repeat again: repeat already means again.
words.prompt: You didn't hear a phone number. Ask the person.
words.model: Sorry, could you repeat the number, please?
qs: Which English words do you need to repeat to remember?
Do you ever repeat the same mistakes?

pl: Powiedzieć albo zrobić coś jeszcze raz.
ro: a repeta
A spune sau a face ceva încă o dată.

words.def: To make it easier for someone to do something.
words.ex: Can I help you with your bags?
words.ex2: Thank you for your help yesterday.
words.watch: Help someone with something, or help someone do something: She helped me carry the box.
words.prompt: Offer help to a tourist who looks lost.
words.model: Excuse me, can I help you? Are you looking for something?
qs: Who helps you most with English?
How do you help people at home?

pl: Sprawiać, że komuś łatwiej coś zrobić.
ro: a ajuta, ajutor
A face să-i fie cuiva mai ușor să facă ceva.

words.def: A small paper or code that shows you have paid to travel or to enter a place.
words.ex: I'd like a ticket to Kraków, please.
words.ex2: Show your ticket at the door.
words.watch: A single ticket is one way; a return ticket is there and back.
words.prompt: Buy a train ticket at a station.
words.model: Good morning. A return ticket to Warsaw, please.
qs: When did you last buy a ticket for something?
Do you buy tickets online or at the station?

pl: Kartka lub kod, który pokazuje, że zapłaciłeś za przejazd albo wstęp.
ro: bilet
O hârtie sau un cod care arată că ai plătit pentru călătorie sau intrare.

words.def: A piece of paper that shows how much you must pay in a restaurant.
coll: could I have the bill, please?
words.ex: Could we have the bill, please?
words.ex2: My father paid the bill.
words.watch: British English: the bill. American English: the check.
words.prompt: Ask the waiter for the bill and to pay by card.
words.model: Excuse me, could I have the bill, please? Can I pay by card?
qs: Who usually pays the bill when you eat out?
Do you like to split the bill with friends?

up.model: Could we have the bill, please?

pl: Kartka, na której jest napisane, ile trzeba zapłacić w restauracji.
ro: nota de plată
Hârtia care arată cât trebuie să plătești la restaurant.

words.def: The number, street and town where a person lives or where a building is.
words.ex: Could you write your address here, please?
words.ex2: What's your email address?
words.watch: Address has two d's and two s's.
words.prompt: Give a taxi driver the address of your hotel.
words.model: Good evening. The address is 12 Long Street, please.
qs: How many times have you changed your address?
Is your email address easy to remember?

pl: Numer, ulica i miasto, gdzie ktoś mieszka albo gdzie jest budynek.
ro: adresă
Numărul, strada și orașul unde locuiește cineva sau unde e o clădire.

words.def: Ready for customers or visitors; not closed.
words.ex: The museum is open from 10 a.m.
words.ex2: Could you open the window, please?
words.watch: The shop is open (adjective), not the shop is opened.
words.prompt: Ask what time a shop is open on Saturday.
words.model: Excuse me, what time are you open on Saturday?
qs: Are shops open on Sundays in your country?
What time does your favourite café open?

pl: Gotowy na klientów lub gości; nie zamknięty.
ro: deschis, a deschide
Gata pentru clienți sau vizitatori; nu închis.

words.def: Not open to customers or visitors.
words.ex: Sorry, the bank is closed now.
words.ex2: The road is closed because of the snow.
words.watch: Closed (adjective) describes the state. Close (verb) is the action: They close at six.
words.prompt: Tell a friend that the restaurant you wanted is not open today.
words.model: Bad news, the restaurant is closed on Mondays.
qs: What is closed on public holidays where you live?
Have you ever arrived somewhere and found it closed?

ro: închis
Care nu e deschis pentru clienți sau vizitatori.

words.def: A friendly, polite thing to say when you leave someone during the day.
coll: you too, have a nice day
have a nice day at work
words.ex: Thank you for shopping with us. Have a nice day!
words.ex2: Have a nice day at school!
words.watch: The usual answer is: Thanks, you too.
words.prompt: Say goodbye to a shop assistant after you pay.
words.model: Thank you very much. Have a nice day!
qs: Who says have a nice day to you?
What makes a nice day for you?

pl: Uprzejme zdanie na pożegnanie w ciągu dnia.
ro: o zi bună
Un lucru politicos și prietenos de spus când pleci, în timpul zilei.

words.def: A strong, polite way to thank someone.
coll: thank you very much, that's kind
words.ex: Thank you very much for your help.
words.ex2: Thank you very much for coming today.
words.watch: Thank you very much for + noun or -ing: Thank you very much for inviting me.
words.prompt: Thank a host for a lovely dinner.
words.model: Thank you very much for dinner. It was delicious.
qs: When did you last say thank you very much?
Do people in your country say thank you often?

pl: Mocny, grzeczny sposób, by komuś podziękować.
ro: mulțumesc foarte mult
Un mod puternic și politicos de a mulțumi cuiva.

words.def: A polite greeting you use before about 12 o'clock.
words.ex: Good morning, Mrs Smith. How are you today?
words.ex2: The teacher said good morning to the class.
words.watch: Use good morning to say hello, not goodbye. To say goodbye at night, say good night.
words.prompt: How do you greet your teacher or your boss when you arrive in the morning?
words.model: I say good morning to my boss when I arrive at work.
qs: Who do you say good morning to every day?
What time do you stop saying good morning?

pl: Grzeczne powitanie używane mniej więcej do godziny 12.
ro: bună dimineața
Salut politicos folosit până pe la ora 12.

words.def: A polite way to show you are happy that someone helped you or gave you something.
words.ex: Thank you for your email, Mr Jones.
words.ex2: Thank you very much for your help.
words.watch: Thank you is two words. Thankyou as one word is a spelling mistake.
words.prompt: Write one polite sentence to thank someone who helped you this week.
words.model: Thank you for helping me with my homework yesterday.
qs: How do you thank a shop assistant in English?
Who was the last person you said thank you to?

pl: Grzeczny sposób, by okazać wdzięczność za pomoc lub prezent.
ro: mulțumesc
Mod politicos de a arăta că ești recunoscător pentru ajutor sau pentru ceva primit.

words.def: A polite phrase to get someone's attention or to ask them to move.
coll: excuse me, where is the station?
words.ex: Excuse me, where is the train station?
words.ex2: Excuse me, can I sit here?
words.watch: Say excuse me before you interrupt or ask a stranger something. Say sorry after you make a mistake.
words.prompt: You are lost in a new city. What do you say to a stranger?
words.model: Excuse me, can you tell me where the museum is?
qs: When do you say excuse me on a bus or a train?
How do you get a waiter's attention politely?

up.model: Excuse me, where is the bank?

pl: Grzeczny zwrot, by zwrócić czyjąś uwagę albo poprosić, żeby ktoś się przesunął.
ro: scuzați-mă
Expresie politicoasă pentru a atrage atenția cuiva sau a-l ruga să se mute.

words.def: A polite way to say what you want.
coll: I would like to book a room
words.ex: I would like a table for two, please.
words.ex2: I would like to book a room for Friday.
words.watch: After would like, use a noun or to + verb: I would like to book a room, not I would like book a room.
words.prompt: You are in a café. Order your favourite drink politely.
words.model: I would like a large cappuccino, please.
qs: What would you like to do this weekend?
Where would you like to travel next year?

up.model: I would like a coffee, please.

pl: Grzeczny sposób, by powiedzieć, czego chcesz.
ro: aș dori
Mod politicos de a spune ce vrei.

words.def: A small word you add to make a request polite.
words.ex: Could you open the window, please?
words.ex2: Please sit down and wait.
words.watch: Put please at the start or the end of a request: Please close the door, or Close the door, please.
words.prompt: Ask a classmate for something you need, politely.
words.model: Could you lend me a pen, please?
qs: How many times do you say please in a normal day?
Is it rude to forget please in your language?

up.model: Could you give me the menu, please?

pl: Krótkie słowo, które sprawia, że prośba brzmi grzecznie.
ro: vă rog / te rog
Un cuvânt mic care face o cerere politicoasă.

words.def: What you say when you leave someone or end a phone call.
words.ex: Goodbye, and thank you for coming.
words.ex2: We said goodbye at the airport.
words.watch: Goodbye sounds a little formal with friends. With friends, bye or see you is more natural.
words.prompt: How do you end a phone call with your doctor or your boss?
words.model: Thank you for your help. Goodbye.
qs: Who did you say goodbye to today?
Is it hard for you to say goodbye at airports?

up.model: Goodbye, and have a nice day.

pl: To, co mówisz, gdy się z kimś żegnasz lub kończysz rozmowę telefoniczną.
ro: la revedere
Ce spui când pleci sau închei o convorbire telefonică.

words.def: A word you say when you have made a small mistake or caused a problem for someone.
words.ex: I'm sorry, I don't understand the question.
words.ex2: Sorry for being late, Mr Green.
words.watch: Say sorry for + -ing: sorry for being late, not sorry for be late.
words.prompt: Write a polite sentence to say sorry to a teacher or a boss.
words.model: I'm sorry, but I can't come to the meeting on Friday.
qs: When did you last say sorry to someone?
What do you say if you step on someone's foot?

pl: Słowo, które mówisz po drobnym błędzie albo gdy komuś sprawiłeś kłopot.
ro: îmi pare rău, scuze
Cuvânt pe care îl spui când ai greșit puțin sau i-ai creat cuiva o problemă.

words.def: A polite word you say when you did not hear what someone said and want them to say it again.
words.ex: Pardon? Can you say that again, please?
words.ex2: Pardon, I didn't hear your name.
words.watch: Pardon? with a rising voice is polite. What? is not polite in formal situations.
words.prompt: You didn't hear a question at the doctor's. What do you say?
words.model: Pardon? Could you repeat the question, please?
qs: What do you say when you can't hear someone on the phone?
Is it polite to say What? to a teacher?

pl: Grzeczne słowo, gdy nie usłyszałeś, co ktoś powiedział, i prosisz o powtórzenie.
ro: poftim? / pardon
Cuvânt politicos când n-ai auzit ce a spus cineva și vrei să repete.
tr.ffpl: Uwaga: pardon? po angielsku to „słucham?”. Polskie „bez pardonu” (bez litości) nie ma z tym związku.

words.def: A polite answer when someone says thank you.
words.ex: Thank you for the coffee. You're welcome.
words.ex2: You're very welcome, Mrs Lee.
words.watch: Write you're (you are) with an apostrophe, not your.
words.prompt: A customer says thank you to you. How do you answer politely?
words.model: You're welcome. Have a nice day.
qs: What do you say when someone thanks you?
What other polite answers to thank you do you know?

pl: proszę bardzo, nie ma za co
ro: cu plăcere
Răspuns politicos când cineva îți mulțumește.

words.def: A polite thing to say when you meet someone for the first time.
words.ex: Hello, I'm Anna. Nice to meet you.
words.ex2: It was very nice to meet you, Mr Brown.
words.watch: Say nice to meet you the first time only. Next time, say nice to see you.
words.prompt: Introduce yourself to a new colleague in two sentences.
words.model: Hello, my name is Tom. Nice to meet you.
qs: Who was the last new person you met?
What do you say after someone says nice to meet you?

up.model: Hello, I'm Tom. Nice to meet you.

pl: Grzeczne zdanie przy pierwszym spotkaniu z kimś.
ro: îmi pare bine de cunoștință
Ce spui politicos când întâlnești pe cineva prima dată.

words.def: A casual way to say hello or to get someone's attention.
words.ex: Hey! Long time no see!
words.ex2: Hey, wait for me!
words.watch: Hey is fine with friends, but too casual for a boss or a stranger in a formal place.
words.prompt: Write a text message to start a chat with a friend.
words.model: Hey! Are you free this evening?
qs: Who do you say hey to?
How do you greet friends in your language?

pl: Luźny sposób, by się przywitać albo zwrócić czyjąś uwagę.
ro: hei, salut
Un mod relaxat de a saluta sau de a atrage atenția cuiva.

words.def: A very friendly, casual hello, common in British English.
words.ex: Hiya! How was your weekend?
words.ex2: She waved and said hiya.
words.watch: Hiya is British and very casual. Don't use it in an email to a client.
words.prompt: Greet a neighbour you know well.
words.model: Hiya! Lovely weather today, isn't it?
qs: Have you heard British people say hiya?
What's your favourite way to say hello?

pl: Bardzo przyjazne, luźne cześć, popularne w Wielkiej Brytanii.
ro: salut (britanic, familiar)
Un salut foarte prietenos și relaxat, des folosit în engleza britanică.

words.def: A casual way to ask someone how they are.
words.ex: Hi, Mark! How's it going?
words.ex2: How's it going with your new job?
words.watch: Short answers are normal: Good, thanks. Not bad.
words.prompt: Ask a friend about their new flat.
words.model: Hey! How's it going in the new flat?
qs: How's it going with your English this month?
How do you answer how's it going on a bad day?

pl: Luźny sposób, by zapytać, co u kogoś słychać.
ro: cum merge?
Un mod relaxat de a întreba pe cineva ce face.

words.def: A casual way to say that something is OK or quite good.
words.ex: How are you? Not bad, thanks.
words.ex2: The pizza was not bad at all.
words.watch: British people often say not bad when they mean good.
words.prompt: Answer a friend who asks about your day.
words.model: Not bad, thanks. A bit tired, but OK.
qs: What was not bad about your week?
Do you say not bad or great more often?

pl: Luźny sposób, by powiedzieć, że coś jest OK albo całkiem dobre.
ro: nu-i rău, merge
Un mod relaxat de a spune că ceva e în regulă sau destul de bun.

words.def: A very casual way to say yes.
words.ex: Are you ready? Yep!
words.ex2: Yep, I'll be there at six.
words.watch: Use yep in speech and texts with friends, never in a job interview.
words.prompt: Reply to a friend's text asking if you're coming to the party.
words.model: Yep, see you there!
qs: Do you use yep in your messages?
What do people say for yes in your language when they're relaxed?

pl: Bardzo luźny sposób, by powiedzieć tak.
ro: da (foarte familiar)
Un mod foarte relaxat de a spune da.

words.def: A very casual way to say no.
words.ex: Have you finished? Nope, not yet.
words.ex2: Nope, I've never been to Spain.
words.watch: Nope can sound a bit cold. Add a reason or sorry to be friendly.
words.prompt: A friend asks if you've seen a new film. You haven't. Reply.
words.model: Nope, not yet. Is it good?
qs: What's something you'd say nope to straight away?
Do you prefer nope or no?

pl: Bardzo luźny sposób, by powiedzieć nie.
ro: nu (foarte familiar)
Un mod foarte relaxat de a spune nu.

words.def: A casual way to say yes or OK.
words.ex: Can you help me? Sure!
words.ex2: Sure, I'll call you later.
words.watch: Are you sure? means are you certain? Sure! alone means yes, happily.
words.prompt: A friend asks to borrow your charger. Answer.
words.model: Sure, here you go.
qs: What do you always say sure to?
Are you sure about your plans for next year?

pl: Luźny sposób, by powiedzieć tak albo OK.
ro: sigur, desigur
Un mod relaxat de a spune da sau OK.

words.def: Pleasant, good or kind.
words.ex: That's a really nice jacket!
words.ex2: Nice one! You passed the test.
words.watch: Nice is very common but simple. For variety, try lovely or great.
words.prompt: Say something good about a friend's new haircut.
words.model: Your hair looks really nice!
qs: What's a nice place in your town?
Who is the nicest person you know?

ro: drăguț, frumos, plăcut
Plăcut, bun sau amabil.

words.def: Enjoyment; or something that is enjoyable.
words.ex: Have fun at the party!
words.ex2: The trip was so much fun.
words.watch: Fun = enjoyable. Funny = makes you laugh. A fun teacher and a funny teacher are different!
words.prompt: Tell a friend about something enjoyable you did last weekend.
words.model: We went bowling on Saturday. It was so much fun!
qs: What do you do for fun?
What's the most fun you've had this year?

pl: Przyjemność; albo coś, co sprawia przyjemność.
ro: distracție, distractiv
Plăcere; sau ceva care îți face plăcere.

words.def: Very nice or beautiful; British people also say it to mean great or thanks.
words.ex: What a lovely day!
words.ex2: Here's your tea. Lovely, thanks!
words.watch: In Britain, lovely! often just means great or OK, thanks.
words.prompt: React to a friend who shows you a photo of their holiday.
words.model: Oh, that's lovely! Where is it?
qs: What's the loveliest place you've visited?
What's lovely about autumn?

pl: Bardzo miły albo piękny; Brytyjczycy mówią tak też zamiast super albo dzięki.
ro: minunat, drăguț
Foarte plăcut sau frumos; britanicii îl folosesc și pentru super sau mersi.

words.def: A friendly word for mother, used in British English.
words.ex: I'm going to call my mum tonight.
words.ex2: Mum, where are my keys?
words.watch: British: mum. American: mom. In formal writing, use mother.

Un cuvânt scurt, de zi cu zi, pentru bicicletă.

Dulapul rece din bucătărie unde ții mâncarea proaspătă.

words.def: A friendly, old-fashioned word for a friend.

words.def: A very short, casual British way to say thank you.

How many ways can you say thanks in English?

Un mod britanic foarte scurt și relaxat de a mulțumi.

words.def: A friendly way to say goodbye that shows you care about the person.

Un mod prietenos de a-ți lua rămas-bun, care arată că îți pasă.

words.def: A casual way to say goodbye to someone you'll see again soon.
words.ex: I've got to go. Catch you later!
words.ex2: Catch you later at the gym.
words.watch: Very casual. With a teacher or boss, say see you later instead.

What other ways of saying goodbye do you know?

up.plain: Goodbye. I will see you soon.

pl: Luźne pożegnanie z kimś, kogo wkrótce zobaczysz.
ro: ne vedem mai târziu, pa
Un mod relaxat de a-ți lua rămas-bun de la cineva pe care îl vei vedea curând.

words.def: What you say when you make a small mistake or drop something.
words.ex: Oops! I spilled my coffee.
words.ex2: Oops, wrong number, sorry!
words.watch: Oops is for small mistakes. For a big problem it sounds too light.

ro: hopa, ups
Ce spui când faci o mică greșeală sau scapi ceva.

words.def: What you say when you are very surprised or impressed.
words.ex: Wow! Your flat is beautiful.
words.ex2: Wow, you speak five languages?
words.watch: Wow alone is a reaction. Add a reason: Wow, that's fast!
words.prompt: React to a friend who says they ran a marathon.
words.model: Wow! How long did it take you?
qs: What made you say wow recently?

pl: To, co mówisz, gdy coś cię bardzo zaskoczy albo zachwyci.
ro: uau
Ce spui când ești foarte surprins sau impresionat.

words.def: A short, friendly way to say hello.

words.ex2: Say hi to your sister for me.

words.def: An informal way to say thank you.

Mod informal de a spune mulțumesc.

ro: da (familiar)
Mod informal de a spune da.

words.def: A short, friendly way to say goodbye.
words.ex: Bye! See you tomorrow.
words.ex2: She said bye and got on the bus.
words.watch: Bye is for friends and family. To a customer or in a formal email, use goodbye or kind regards.
words.prompt: End a phone call with your best friend.
words.model: OK, bye! Talk to you later.
qs: How do you say bye in your language when you're in a hurry?
Do you say bye or goodbye to your teacher?

pl: Krótki, przyjazny sposób, by się pożegnać.
ro: pa
Un mod scurt și prietenos de a-ți lua rămas-bun.

words.def: Very good, fashionable or great.

Foarte bun, la modă sau grozav.

words.def: An informal way to say yes, all right or fine.

words.ex2: That's great news!

ro: nicio problemă

Un mod prietenos de a saluta sau de a întreba un prieten ce face.

words.def: To plan or organise something, for example a meeting or a trip.

Who suggests the best ideas at work?

Do you appreciate your town more now than as a child?

How many emails do you receive in a day?

A permite oficial cuiva să facă ceva.

A te întâlni cu un prieten ca să vorbiți despre ce s-a mai întâmplat.

words.def: To send an email or letter you have received to another person.

words.def: More or additional; used a lot in formal emails.

words.def: A formal way to say before.

Un mod formal de a spune înainte de.

words.def: To make certain that something happens or is true.

A face sigur că ceva se întâmplă sau e adevărat.

words.def: Buildings, rooms or equipment provided for a particular use.

words.def: A place to live or stay, such as a hotel room or flat.

Un loc unde să locuiești sau să stai, cum ar fi o cameră de hotel.

Why do people jump the gun with big news?

pl: Zrobić coś za wcześnie, przed właściwym momentem.
ro: a se grăbi, a sări peste etape
A face ceva prea devreme, înainte de momentul potrivit.

words.def: An obvious, important problem that everyone avoids talking about.
coll: address the elephant in the room
ignore the elephant in the room
the elephant in the room is money
words.ex: Money was the elephant in the room at the meeting.
words.ex2: Let's address the elephant in the room: we're behind schedule.
words.watch: Address the elephant in the room means to finally talk about it.
words.prompt: Describe a problem everyone in a group knew about but nobody mentioned.
words.model: The elephant in the room was that nobody had read the report.
qs: What is the elephant in the room in your workplace or school?
Why do people avoid the elephant in the room?

up.model: Nobody mentions the elephant in the room.

pl: Oczywisty, ważny problem, o którym wszyscy unikają rozmowy.
ro: elefantul din cameră
O problemă evidentă și importantă despre care toți evită să vorbească.

words.def: To blame or sacrifice someone else to protect yourself.
coll: throw a colleague under the bus
words.ex: When the project failed, he threw his team under the bus.
words.ex2: I felt thrown under the bus by my manager.
words.watch: Put the person in the middle: throw your boss under the bus. The past is threw.
words.prompt: Describe a time someone blamed another person to save themselves.
words.model: She threw me under the bus to avoid getting into trouble.
qs: Have you ever been thrown under the bus?
Why do politicians throw advisers under the bus?

up.plain: He blamed his colleague to protect himself.
up.model: He threw his colleague under the bus.

pl: zrzucić winę na kogoś, poświęcić kogoś
Obwinić lub poświęcić kogoś innego, żeby chronić siebie.
ro: a da pe cineva la o parte, a-l sacrifica
A da vina pe altcineva sau a-l sacrifica pentru a te proteja.

words.def: A task that is very difficult or unreasonable to ask for.
coll: a bit of a tall order
words.ex: Finishing the report by tomorrow is a tall order.
words.ex2: Learning a language in a month is quite a tall order.
words.watch: A big ask means the same and is just as informal.
words.prompt: Describe a task someone asked you to do that was nearly impossible.
words.model: Cooking for thirty people alone was a tall order.
qs: What is a tall order for you at work or school?
Is fluent English in a year a tall order?

pl: Zadanie bardzo trudne albo nierozsądne, by o nie prosić.
ro: o sarcină grea
O sarcină foarte grea sau nerezonabilă.

words.def: To accept something unpleasant that you can no longer avoid.
words.ex: I finally bit the bullet and booked the dentist.
words.ex2: We'll have to bite the bullet and raise prices.
words.watch: The past is bit: I bit the bullet yesterday.
words.prompt: Describe something unpleasant you finally decided to do.
words.model: I bit the bullet and told my boss I was leaving.
qs: What have you been putting off that you should bite the bullet on?
When did you last bite the bullet?

up.plain: I accepted it and did it.

pl: Zaakceptować coś nieprzyjemnego, czego nie da się już uniknąć.
ro: a strânge din dinți
A accepta ceva neplăcut pe care nu-l mai poți evita.

words.def: Something that takes attention away from the real issue, sometimes on purpose.
coll: turn out to be a red herring
words.ex: The missing key was a red herring; the thief came through the window.
words.ex2: Talk of the budget is a red herring: the real problem is staff.
words.watch: Common in detective stories and debates.
words.prompt: Describe something in a film, book or debate that distracted from the real issue.
words.model: The butler in the film was a red herring; the real killer was the gardener.
qs: Can you think of a red herring in a crime story?
Why do debaters use red herrings?

up.plain: That's not the real issue; it's a distraction.

pl: Coś, co odciąga uwagę od prawdziwego problemu, czasem celowo.
ro: o pistă falsă
Ceva care distrage atenția de la problema reală, uneori intenționat.

words.def: To avoid saying something directly, usually because it is uncomfortable.
words.ex: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what happened.
words.ex2: She didn't beat around the bush: she said the plan wouldn't work.
words.watch: British English often says beat about the bush.
words.prompt: Ask someone to say something directly.
words.model: Don't beat around the bush; just tell me if I got the job.
qs: Do people in your culture beat around the bush?
When is it kinder to beat around the bush?

pl: Unikać mówienia czegoś wprost, zwykle bo to niezręczne.
ro: a o lua pe ocolite
A evita să spui ceva direct, de obicei pentru că e incomod.

words.def: To talk about the most important thing immediately, without unnecessary details.
words.ex: Let's cut to the chase: how much will it cost?
words.ex2: I'll cut to the chase. We need more money.
words.watch: Cut to the chase comes from old films that skipped to the car chase.
words.prompt: Start an important conversation directly in one sentence.
words.model: To cut to the chase, we need two more people on the team.
qs: When do you prefer people to cut to the chase?
Is it rude to cut to the chase in your language?

up.plain: Let's talk about the main point now.

pl: Od razu mówić o najważniejszym, bez zbędnych szczegółów.
ro: a trece la subiect
A vorbi imediat despre lucrul cel mai important, fără detalii inutile.
